fallacies.name: Straw man
fallacies.what: Attacking a twisted, weaker version of what someone said instead of their real view.
fallacies.example: “You want remote-first? So you think people should never meet again!”
fallacies.tip: Ask: is that really what they claimed?

fallacies.name: Ad hominem
fallacies.what: Rejecting an argument by attacking the person making it.
fallacies.example: “Why listen to her? She failed her exams.”
fallacies.tip: Judge the reasons, not the reasoner (unless they're giving testimony).

fallacies.name: You only say that because…
fallacies.what: Dismissing a claim by pointing at the speaker's motives or situation.
fallacies.example: “You only argue for remote work because you hate commuting.”
fallacies.tip: A motive doesn't make an argument false.

fallacies.name: Tu quoque (you too!)
fallacies.what: Rejecting advice because the advisor doesn't follow it.
fallacies.example: “You tell me to exercise, but you never do!”
fallacies.tip: Hypocrisy says something about the person, not about the claim.

fallacies.example: “That idea came from that club, so it must be wrong.”

fallacies.example: “He got the idea from a dream, so it can't be right.”
